title: Pay halted for suspended Vancouver police officer charged with fraud and theft
summary: The Vancouver Police Board has discontinued pay for a high-profile officer accused of fraud and theft.

image.caption: Vancouver police officer Kal Dosanjh is pictured walking down a Vancouver sidewalk on Dec. 12, 2018. (Jon Hernandez/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
The Vancouver Police Board has discontinued pay for a high-profile officer accused of fraud and theft.
Kal Dosanjh was suspended in September amid fraud, theft and breach of trust charges

Const. Kal Dosanjh is facing multiple charges, including fraud over $5,000, theft over $5,000 and breach of trust, related to allegations he defrauded about $19 million from 19 victims, dating back to 2017.
Dosanjh denies all of the allegations.
Dosanjh was suspended in September. At the time, Chief Const. Steve Rai said he was recommending that Dosanjh be suspended without pay.
In a statement posted on Friday, the police board said it had deliberated, reviewed Dosanjh's submission, and decided to discontinue his pay and allowances for the duration of his suspension.
The move does not affect his benefits.
High-profile VPD officer Kal Dosanjh faces fraud, theft charges
In September, Rai said police began investigating Dosanjh in 2023 after multiple alleged victims came forward.

According to court documents, the multiple charges relate to allegations of fraud and theft from investors in the Azura, Queen's Park and Sahara development projects, as well as his work for the KidsPlay Youth Foundation, which he founded in 2015.
In September, Dosanjh released a statement through his lawyer maintaining his innocence.
"I deny the allegations against me and I look forward to defending myself fully in court," the 26-year Vancouver police veteran said.
"I will allow the evidence and the facts to speak for themselves."

blocks.text: His lawyer, Joven Narwal, also questioned the integrity of the investigation, noting it was led by the VPD.
"That raises legitimate concerns about investigative independence, objectivity and the safeguards used when a police department investigates one of its own members," he said.
Rai has said that the VPD handled the investigation after consulting with the RCMP because it was best equipped with the expertise and resources to handle the file.
CBC News has requested comment about the pay suspension from Dosanjh through his lawyer, but has yet to receive a response.
None of the allegations have been proven in court.
Dosanjh's next court date is scheduled for Dec. 3.
